what: Fresenius Medical Care treats kidney failure. It runs about 4,000 dialysis clinics worldwide, most of them in the United States, and it also makes the dialysis machines and filters used in them.
customers: Patients with end-stage kidney disease, paid for by Medicare, insurers and national health systems.
money: running dialysis clinics, mostly in the United States
dialysis machines, dialysers and solutions sold worldwide
moat: A clinic network near where patients live, because dialysis means travelling three times a week, combined with being one of two companies that make the machines.
risks: Medicare rates set most of the revenue and rise more slowly than nurse wages
GLP-1 weight loss drugs may slow the growth of diabetes-related kidney failure, which is the main source of patients
opportunities: 5.7 times free cash flow with $2.0B of free cash flow against an $11.2B market value
Revenue grew from $20.1B to $23.1B last year
A multi-year cost programme has raised the margin and treatment volumes are recovering
watch: Same-market treatment growth in the United States and the operating margin.
